fuels.quote: Using the experimental conditions of FLEX flight, a comparative studies of the oxygen concentration effects on the extinction limits of cool flames was conducted using three different numerical modeling schemes, (a) spark-assisted flame propagation of a n-heptane/air mixture, (b) one dimensional freely-propagating dimethyl ether (DME) flames using an arc-length continuation method and (c) simulated cool flame regimes and burning limits at elevated pressure (up to 20 atm) using DME/air mixtures.

Using the experimental conditions of FLEX flight, a comparative studies of the oxygen concentration effects on the extinction limits of cool flames was conducted using three different numerical modeling schemes, (a) spark-assisted flame propagation of a n-heptane/air mixture, (b) one dimensional freely-propagating dimethyl ether (DME) flames using an arc-length continuation method and (c) simulated cool flame regimes and burning limits at elevated pressure (up to 20 atm) using DME/air mixtures.

Specific research details are outlined in the publication, ''Dynamics of cool flames'' [https://doi.org/10.1016/j.pecs.2019.100787]; '' Understanding Cool Flames and Warm Flames'', [https://doi.org/10.1016/j.proci.2020.09.019] and ''Study of the low-temperature reactivity of large n-alkanes through cool diffusion flame extinction'', [https://doi.org/10.1016/j.combustflame.2017.01.028].

objective_summary.value: The purpose of this investigation was to use FLEX microgravity experimental data, numerical modeling, and ground-based ozone-sensitized counterflow flame experiments to study cool flame flammability and extinction limits. It aimed to bridge the understanding between hot and cool flame limits while validating kinetic and radiation models.

key_findings.value: Warm flames feature a double reaction zone structure essential for transitioning between cool and hot flames. Additionally, elevated pressures expand the flammable region of warm and cool flames by increasing low- and intermediate-temperature reactivity.
key_findings.quote: The results showed that the warm flame has a double reaction zone structure and plays a critical role in the transition between cool flames and hot flames.

earth_applications.value: Cool and warm flame regimes are relevant to high-pressure near-limit combustion applications on Earth because many real engines operate in the 20-40 atm pressure range.
earth_applications.quote: Since many real engines operate in the 20-40 atm pressure range, therefore, cool flames and warm flames are relevant and important flame regimes for high-pressure near-limit combustion applications.
